learnedInvalidAssumptions: 2026-08-12 via STUDY-IVTOUCH-DIR-2026-08-12: PM YES trading above the options touch model is tradeable richness on downside barriers ("dip to", "hit (LOW)"). It is not: across 27 gated downside entries the market was calibrated (45.3% priced vs 44.4% realised touch) while the model underpriced touch by 11pt, so the apparent richness was model error and selling it returned -24.0% per trade at a 33% win rate. Only upside barriers carry a real premium to fade (29.3% priced vs 9.1% realised, +10.6% per trade over 22 entries).

2026-08-12 via STUDY-IVTOUCH-DIR-2026-08-12: An edge-compression exit protects a rich-NO barrier position. It does not: the model's touch probability rises alongside the market's as spot approaches the barrier, so the gap compresses at or after the worst mark on 80% of paths (mean mark at compression -4.8% vs -11.7% worst on path). It is a lagging indicator of a loss, not a stop.
